From the get go you are thrown into the games story line and it does not stop. The pacing does not allow you to sink your teethe in to what I thought would be a fun and interesting game play loop. 
Instead of playing an agent who starts to slowly unravel a conspiracy through your own investigations and discoveries, you are just railroaded into it by the characters that force themselves on you.
I really like on the surface what they put together. The presentation is fantastic; but for me the pacing of it all just threw me off.

review_text_raw: Great concept with the same bad execution that Hypnospace Outlaw suffers from. Great ideas behind the design and concept of the game, but you're not really solving any hard mysteries, just solving some (admittedly cool) puzzles as a story shoves itself in your face. The pacing is terrible - you don't get time to immerse yourself in what would otherwise be nice gameplay. This is hardly a "game" more than it is an interactive visual novel, that is to say that you don't really think critically beyond puzzles and so forth.

review_text_raw:
My experience with The Operator can be summed up as follows: great presentation, limited investigation.  It's a  game that looks sharp, feels polished, and tells a story that is rather entertaining, yet never quite trusts you enough to truly investigate it on your own. I enjoyed my time with it. I just kept wishing it would let me off the leash.

The production is slick from top to bottom. The performances sell the drama, and the narrative momentum keeps you moving even when a few plot holes start to peek through if you linger too long on the details. It is a fun story. It just is not a particularly demanding one.

Let’s be clear about something. This is not really an investigation game.

You are deliberately guided from one beat to the next with little room to wander or hope oiff the beaten path. That keeps the pacing tight, sure, but it also strips away the thrill of deduction that hallmarks great detective games . No alternate paths, no clever lateral thinking moments, no opportunities to feel like you outsmarted the system. Outside of one genuinely challenging, spoiler free sequence that actually made me pause and think, most of the puzzles feel straightforward and simple to resolve.

And then there is the ending. I assumed I had stumbled into the Bad Ending because of something I had done wrong, only to realize that this was simply... the finish. And I figured it was disappointing.

This game didn't scratch my detective game itch. I love having my detective instincts tested. I enjoy piecing together clues and trusting my logic to guide me. I wanted more depth, more resistance. That said, for someone easing into detective style games for the first time, this is an excellent starting point. As long as you're picking it up on sale.

review_text_raw:
This game has potential, but it's just not there yet. 

There are QoL improvements that would be great, like a copy and paste ability. 
The PM sequences are painful to get through. I thought something was wrong with my game the first time. 
The story was very predictable while still managing to be convoluted and note fully fleshed out. 
There are some great tools that are introduced in the game, like an analysis kit or a bomb diffuser but you only use them once. 
The pacing is very very slow. I kept playing because I hoped the ending would be worth it. Unfortunately, it was not.
